title: Reservation risk scoring and safety-buffering playbook for Dedicated capacity
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a pragmatic, auditable playbook that ties reservation intake to an automated risk score and a safety-buffer provisioning policy. The goal is to reduce manual approval friction for low-risk Dedicated capacity requests while ensuring fleet stability and predictable throughput guarantees. The playbook will define risk signals, buffer sizing rules, provisional (trial) capacity lanes, and escalation policies that integrate with the existing provisioning and billing systems.
background: Current intake for Dedicated reservations is heavily manual and conservative: many requests require full ops review even when the customer is low-risk and the requested throughput is within fleet headroom. This increases lead time for customers, slows sales handoffs, and concentrates load on the provisioning squad. We need a repeatable policy that balances safety (protect SLAs for existing tenants) and speed (reduce time-to-reservation for predictable requests).
proposed_workflow: 1) Request submission: customer fills reservation form with throughput profile, 30/60/90 day forecast, spike tolerance, and business justification. 2) Automated risk scoring: system calculates a Risk Score (0-100) using signals: historical usage, billing standing, region affinity, model type (large vs small), burstiness metric, and requested commit vs forecast. 3) Buffer assignment: map Risk Score + requested throughput to a safety buffer multiplier (e.g., low-risk -> 10% buffer; medium -> 25%; high -> 50%) and a provisional burst credit allowance. 4) Fast-path approvals: requests with Risk Score <= 25 and buffer-adjusted capacity <= continuous headroom are auto-approved and placed in 'provisional' state for 14 days. 5) Provisional monitoring: telemetry checks for retention, overages, and test traffic patterns; automated rollback if anomalies detected. 6) Ops review for high-risk or headroom-critical requests with pre-populated dossier (score, signals, suggested buffer). 7) Final binding: convert provisional to committed reservation after the probation window and required contract sign-off. 8) Post-commit adjustments: defined cadence for re-evaluating buffers and scaling policies (monthly and at usage milestones).
acceptance_criteria: Automated intake computes a Risk Score and safety buffer in >= 90% of submissions without human intervention.
Low-risk requests (<25 score) that fit current headroom are auto-approved within 15 minutes and placed in provisional state.
Provisional reservations have an automated 14-day monitoring job; any of the three defined anomaly triggers (sustained >x% bursting, >2x forecast, or billing arrears) cause immediate alert and hold.
Ops dashboard adds a reservation dossier with key signals and the calculated buffer for reviewers.
Run a pilot with 10 customers and measure median lead time reduction vs baseline (target: 60% faster approval).
Documented playbook, runbook, and handoff checklist published to the Ranger Confluence space and linked to the provisioning runbook.
decision_log: 2026-02-18 Maya Chen: Proposed risk signals and buffer multipliers for initial review.
2026-02-24 Engineering review (Rajiv Singh): Recommended adding model architecture as a weighted signal and capping provisional burst at 30% of requested throughput.
2026-03-03 Security review (Priya Patel): No sensitive data required by model signals; recommended include KMS status as a gating flag for enterprise customers.
2026-03-10 Product sync (Luca Moretti): Agreed on 14-day probation window and pilot cohort selection criteria.
implementation_notes: Risk scoring will live in the provisioning service as a stateless function; inputs are the intake form + lookup calls to billing and usage APIs.
Ops dashboard needs a new 'reservation dossier' UI block showing score, top contributing signals, and buffer recommendation.
Billing integration: provisional reservations should accrue but be marked as non-invoiceable until conversion, with flags for finance to review usage during probation.
A/B test plan: route 50% of qualifying low-risk requests through the fast-path for the pilot month to validate safety and lead-time improvements.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Auto-approvals could oversubscribe hot regions. Mitigation: include regional headroom as a hard gating signal and fail closed when headroom < safety-threshold.

Risk: Customers may intentionally under-forecast to get auto-approval. Mitigation: probation monitoring with chargebacks applied on conversion if sustained overusage is detected; limit frequency of auto-approvals per account.
Risk: Incorrect signals lead to noisy ops alerts. Mitigation: start pilot with conservative buffer multipliers and a small customer cohort; tune signal weights after 4 weeks.
